definitions.explanation: A social class designation established in the early Meiji era for families of former samurai. After the abolition of the feudal class system, samurai families were officially reclassified as shizoku, a status that was maintained in family registers until 1947.

examples.japanese: ⟦{明治|めいじ}{維新|いしん}→明治維新：16286_meijiishin⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{武士|ぶし}→武士：03989_bushi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{士族|しぞく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: With the Meiji Restoration, samurai became shizoku.

examples.japanese: {士族|しぞく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{反乱|はんらん}→反乱：11860_hanran⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{各地|かくち}→各地：00155_kakuchi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{起|お}きた→起きる：00521_okiru⟧。
examples.english: Shizoku rebellions broke out across the country.

examples.japanese: ⟦{特権|とっけん}→特権：13499_tokken⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{失|うしな}った→失う：01887_ushinau⟧{士族|しぞく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{多|おお}く⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{経済的|けいざいてき}→経済的：05675_keizaiteki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{困窮|こんきゅう}→困窮：12018_konkyuu⟧し、⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{職業|しょくぎょう}→職業：03245_shokugyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{探|さが}さなければ→探す：00493_sagasu⟧⟦ならなかった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Many shizoku who lost their privileges fell into economic hardship and had to find new occupations.

notes:
USAGE:
A historical term from the Meiji period (1868–1912). The Meiji government abolished the feudal class system and reclassified the population as {華族|かぞく} (peerage/former nobility), {士族|しぞく} (former samurai), and {平民|へいみん} (commoners).

The expression {士族|しぞく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{商法|しょうほう}→商法：30086_shouhou⟧ (a samurai's way of doing business) is an idiom describing amateurish business practices by former samurai who had no experience with commerce.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {士族|しぞく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{反乱|はんらん}→反乱：11860_hanran⟧: shizoku rebellion
- {士族|しぞく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{商法|しょうほう}→商法：30086_shouhou⟧: amateurish business (idiom)
- {士族|しぞく}{授産|じゅさん}: relief programs for former samurai
